coverage.r1: 00:53-04:00 is an English chat about a song; all Arabic there is redacted as [foreign language] so her explanations (balad/bilad, the 'house yard' word, 5ubza) cannot be quoted - one tier-0 row only. Speaking practice is 06:26-10:40 plus two short productions inside the drill (38:13 'don't be excited yet', 44:46 'bored'). 11:13-1:00:35 is a listening drill: Amal reads Arabic, Medi translates to English; his misreads are written with mode=listening. Many Medi drill turns are garbled echoes ('Kamara', 'Tawamara', 'Namaste', 'Bisar') = him repeating/mishearing, not scored. 09:15 خمارة and 10:31 خندرة (for ريحة/كندرة) treated as mishearing/S4 pronunciation, not vocab. 10:08 he self-switched بلوز to 2amees before she typed it, so not a row. Chat lines that just transcribe items he read right were not written. Later CHAT lines (1:02:22-1:04:26) are the drill items typed after the call. medi_turns counts Medi turns containing Arabic or an Arabic attempt (33 in the speaking block, ~36 echoes/productions inside the drill); his ~60 English translation answers in the drill are not counted in that figure.
coverage.r2: Speaking proper is only 06:26-10:49 (date, time, weather, clothes) plus a few asides (37:57-38:24 'don't be excited yet', 41:10 'inti kharabti il safra', 44:46 'bored', 1:00:47 'ahsan katir iliyom'). 11:13 to 1:00:35 is a listening drill: Amal says a verb form, Medi translates to English; every misread there is mode=listening. 00:00-06:25 English chat about a song (Amal's Arabic shows as [foreign language], unreadable). Several Medi echo lines are Latin garble by the engine (Kamara / Kamamara / Tawamara = 'kamm marra' = once more; 'Namaste', 'Aloo', 'Bill', 'Longo', 'Ma bistah') - not scored. Transcript prints enbasa6u/enbasa6tu and enbasa6tillo/enbasa6etlo identically in Arabic, so person reads there lean on her chat lines. 08:54 '2ab el-mbaare7' dropped-2 and 10:31 'khundara' for kundara treated as S4 pronunciation. His self-fix bluze -> 2amees (10:08) not written. medi_turns = ~45 Medi turns containing Arabic + ~70 English translation answers in the drill.

r3_note: From 11:13 to ~1:00:35 the lesson is a listening drill (Amal says an Arabic sentence, Medi translates); rows there are mode listening. Her Arabic in the first 3 minutes is redacted as [foreign language]. Two disputes (D3 and D4) are one moment with two different wrong pieces: D3 is kept for the clipped/MSA form of 19, D4 for the month 6-for-9; the r2 half of D3 is the same slip as D4 and is settled there. D2 and D3 are two separate attempts at the same word (19) with two separate fixes from her, so both stand. Nothing added.

rows.medi_said: Does balad mean like bilad? Like, balad.
rows.amal_said: [foreign language] is one, [foreign language] is multiple. ... I traveled the world.
rows.right: balad = one country, bilad = countries (her explanation; her Arabic is redacted)
rows.why: Didn't-know, not an error: he asked what balad is next to bilad (from the song) and she explained singular vs plural; sheet has only 'country | Dawle', so it is a new word for him.
rows.english: does balad mean the same as bilad (country / countries)?
rows.r3_why: Real didn't-know: he asked about a word and she supplied the meaning (tier 0, signal asked). Her Arabic is redacted as [foreign language] so the row cannot quote it; confidence medium.

rows.medi_said: This is it today. تسعة عشرين.
rows.why: For the 19th he said tis3a 3ishrin (nine-twenty), a non-word for 19; she prompted with '19.', he moved to MSA tes3a 3ashar at 06:42, and her chat spelled the Levantine tese3ta3sh; sheet 'nineteen | tese3ta3sh | تسعتاش'.
rows.r3_why: Both readers saw the slip; it is a wrong number word, not a rule from buckets.md (E4 covers days/months/'on Monday', not how 19 is built), so vocab-A. 'tis3a 3ishrin' is a made-up word for 19 -> tier 1.

rows.medi_said: um, ألفين وسبعة عشرين.
rows.right: ألفين وستة وعشرين (alfain u sitte u 3eshreen) - my reading
rows.why: For the year 2026 he said alfain u sab3a 3eshreen (seven, and no u before the tens), twice identically (06:49, 07:03); she said ممتاز at 06:56 and let it pass. Wrong number word if real; low because she is attentive to numbers and it could be a transcript garble.
rows.r3_why: Real if the transcript is right: sab3a for sitte is a wrong number word (vocab tier 1), and the missing u is a secondary slip with no bucket (E1 does not cover units-u-tens). Repeated identically twice so probably not ASR; kept low for Amal to confirm.

rows.medi_said: تسعش or تسعش. ... تسعش ستة.
rows.why: Second attempt at 19: after MSA tes3a 3ashar (06:42, 07:15) he clipped it to tes3ash; she recast the Levantine tese3ta3sh and typed it; a wrong form of a number he knows, sheet 'nineteen | tese3ta3sh | تسعتاش'.
rows.r3_why: r1 and r2 wrote different pieces for this moment. r1's piece (clipped/MSA 19 recast to tese3ta3sh) is a separate slip from D2 (different wrong form, separate fix at 07:12) and is kept here. r2's piece (month sitte for tes3a) is the same slip r1 filed as D4 and is settled under D4.

rows.medi_said: I said, uh, ستة عشر ستة ... تسعش ستة.
rows.why: He gave the month as sitte (6) at 06:59 and 07:10 for September (9); she queried 'ستة؟' at 07:04, recast tese3ta3sh tes3a at 07:12 and typed it; he still said تسعة عشر ستة at 07:15. Wrong number word.
rows.r3_why: Real and clear in the transcript: wrong number word for the month, she queried it and recast it, he repeated the error. r2 filed the same slip inside D3; one row here covers both.

rows.medi_said: ألفين تنين وتلات.

rows.r3_why: Both readers saw the same slip; the piece he explicitly weighed and got wrong was the el- on mbaare7, and her recast removed it. A prefix rule from buckets.md is grammar (A1), not vocab tier 2. 'أب' for 2abel is a dropped-letter slip (S4).

rows.r3_why: Real listening misread of make-X vs get-X (B12) that she let pass; kept low because her own acceptance of 'is sad' for بيزعل at 20:39 suggests she does not count this gloss. Amal to confirm.

rows.english: did you get annoyed by what happened?
rows.r3_why: A distinct piece from the agreed sad->annoyed slip at 24:10: tense misread of a past verb. Her full recast in the past is a fix by the brief's definition, but her Mm-hmm was acceptance, so confidence low; merger may prefer grammar-B.

rows.why: He read ضايقك first as 'mad at you' and then as 'be upset'; she prompted on the make-vs-get form until he gave 'who made you upset' at 28:17.

rows.why: He heard معنا as منا; she recast 'With us. معنا' and he said 'whoops, I was saying mina'.

rows.why: He read past تحمستِ as present 'are you excited'; she recast to 'did you get excited' and he took it.

rows.medi_said: Why are you tired?
rows.why: laish mut3eb (why is it tiring) read as 'tired' (ta3baan); she repeated mut3eb and asked 'what's tired', he fixed to 'why is it tiring'; sheet rows: 'tiring | Mut3eb | متعب', 'tired | Ta3baan | تعبان'.

rows.medi_said: bizah. ... Is it zar-zarha, zar'a?
rows.amal_said: Yeah. That's boring. ... زهقان. Of course it's that's it. It's بس زهق، زهق.
rows.why: Asked 'what's bored?' he gave the verb beyzahhe2 (she: 'that's boring'), then could not reach the adjective; she supplied zah2aan. Verb used for the adjective = wrong form of a word he knows; sheet 'bored | Zahqaan | زهقان' and 'boring / causes boredom | beyzahheq | بيزهق'.
rows.r3_why: Both readers saw the same slip; the brief files 'verb used as a noun/adjective' under vocab tier 2, and the fix was a whole different word shape, not an ending rule, so vocab-A tier 2 rather than grammar B15. She told him it was the wrong word ('that's boring') before supplying the right one -> explicit-no.

rows.medi_said: Not it as a don't be angry.

rows.medi_said: uh, don't be annoyed.

rows.medi_said: She was happy. ... I enjoyed to it. No, Aloo, uh, Bill. Are you saying Bill?
rows.amal_said: No، انبسطت له. انبسطت له. Just the verb. I got happy له. ... For، for him.
rows.right: I got happy for him (انبسطت له)
rows.why: Listening: he first dropped the -lo, then read la- as 'to it'; she said no, just the verb plus له = 'for him', and he fixed to 'I got happy for him' at 50:53. The preposition after انبسط sets the meaning (له for / معه with / منه because of - all drilled this lesson), so it is the verb's partner preposition.
rows.english: I (or she) got happy for him
rows.r3_why: Same slip in both readers, only the bucket differs. This lesson drilled انبسط + له / معه / منه / لي as meaning-changing partners of the verb, which is D2 (verb + its fixed preposition); D1 kept as bucket2. The 'she' reading was not wrong (she offered enbasa6etlo too), the preposition was.
